newsitem.title: UK: Thames, United up as bid focus shifts.
newsitem.headline: Thames, United up as bid focus shifts.

text.p: Shares in Thames Water Plc and United Utilities Plc rose in a strong UK market on Friday as the flurry of takeover bids in the electricity sector spilled over into water stocks, analysts said.

"The bid story never really goes away," said Angela Whelan, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing. "And there is more and more focus on water companies." At 1246 GMT Thames Water was up 14-1/2p, or 2.5 percent, at 603-1/2 while United Utilities rose 13p, or 2.2 percent, to 606-1/2. The FTSE 100 index was up 32.5 points, or 0.8 percent, at 4083.8 after opening at an all-time high.
Some analysts said they saw potential U.S. bidders increasingly eyeing the UK water sector.
"Even the bigger UK water companies aren't all that big if large U.S. companies are looking to make an offer," said Whelan.

Charterhouse Tilney analyst Simon Champion said: "I think the water sector will go up. U.S. firms looking to acquire UK utility companies are shifting their attention from recs (regional electricity companies) to water companies."
But Champion said the rise also had a lot to do with the strong market in general. "United Utilities went down an awful lot last week, and now it's bouncing back."
